intro_html: Horseradish and beef have been a pairing since long before anybody wrote it down, and a slow cooker is where that pairing gets easy. The heat mellows over eight hours into something warm rather than sharp, the mushrooms go deep and savory, and the gravy ends up creamy without a drop of cream. Each bowl carries 50 grams of protein and 727 calories for about $5.41 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $5.41 a bowl (at everyday cost). Mushrooms and a jar of horseradish sauce are what separate this from a plain pot roast, and neither one is expensive.
shop_smart: White button mushrooms cost a fraction of what the specialty varieties run and they behave better in a long braise anyway. Buy the sealed packs, not the loose bin, when the price is close.
Creamy horseradish sauce keeps for months in the fridge and a jar covers more than one batch. Check the label to be sure you are buying the sauce and not the straight prepared root.
Worcestershire sauce shows up in half the beef recipes here. One bottle covers a year of cooking.
Chuck roast, bought on the sale cycle, is the single biggest lever on this recipe's cost. Nothing else on the list moves the number much.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt, black pepper, and oregano, and sear it in the vegetable oil until it is well browned all over.
Move the roast to the slow cooker and scatter the chopped onion around it.
Whisk the horseradish sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and beef broth together and pour it over the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours.
Add the sliced mushrooms in the last hour so they hold some texture instead of dissolving.
Shred the beef in the cooker with two forks and stir it through the horseradish gravy.
Cook the rice separately and taste the gravy for salt before you portion.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of beef, mushrooms, and gravy into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Each bowl lands at 727 calories with 50 grams of protein.
